{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the hit cap is counted before the branch-scope filter — the default scope under-delivers and pages O(n²)**

`seeRecord` stops at `query.maxHits` hits in `_hits`, but `finish()` only then filters to the active branch. Since `branch` is the **default** scope, every match on an abandoned fork consumes budget and can trigger a premature `result cap` that returns far fewer than 40 branch hits — or zero — while reporting `truncated: true`. Worse, the continuation token skips records globally, so each next page re-scans the entire prefix of the chain: paging through a fork-heavy giant session is O(n²) under a 10 s budget.

No test covers branch-scope + cap together (the seeded fork record doesn't match the test query, so the E4 test can't see this).

Directions: collect hits with branch membership decided at collection time where possible, or over-collect with slack and continue scanning when the branch-filtered count is below the cap; alternatively exclude non-branch hits from the cap accounting and document that a capped branch scan may re-examine fork hits on the next page.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment06.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the E5 "never a hang" guarantee is not enforceable — one record can blow the wall-clock budget**

The comment frames this cap as the E5 DoS bound, but a text-length cap is not a time bound on a backtracking regex engine (the Dart VM's `RegExp` backtracks — catastrophic patterns like `(a+)+$` over the 128 KB record are effectively unbounded). The time-budget check (`checkDeadline`) only runs **between** lines/blocks, never inside `pattern.hasMatch`, so a single pathological match on one giant record wedges the tool call — and the cancel token is not consulted during `execute` either — far beyond the promised 10 s, producing a hung agent rather than an "honest `truncated` report".

This matters more here than for a plain grep tool because the regex comes from the model itself, which routinely emits accidentally-quadratic patterns, and this PR's headline scenario is giant records.

Directions: bound the regex subject far smaller (a match over the first N KB of the record's preview-sized excerpt is enough for a pointer), or run the match in an isolate that can be abandoned on deadline expiry, or explicitly scope the E5 claim down to "budget checked between records" and cap per-record regex input accordingly.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment07.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: accumulator state grows linearly with archive size — the flat-memory claim (E4) does not hold**

`scanSessionSegment`'s doc claims "memory stays flat regardless of file size (E4)", and that is true only for the block/carry streaming. The accumulator itself retains per-record state for the whole chain: `_parentOf` for **every** record id (plus `_ordinalOf` in map mode, doubling it). For a multi-GB archive — this PR's explicit target — with a few million records this is hundreds of MB of id→parent pairs held for the entire scan, and it also accumulates identically on every continuation page.

Directions: the branch walk only needs parents of records on the leaf→root path. Since `RangedReadFileSystem` supports ranged reads, consider a two-pass approach (find the leaf in pass 1 storing only checkpoint/parent facts sparsely, then walk backwards in ranges), or keep parents only for records at/after the last observed fork, or correct the doc comment to state the linear bound honestly and decide whether it is acceptable for the E4 giant-session scenario.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment08.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the human-readable outcome of `recordPendingWait` is constructed and then discarded**

`recordPendingWait`'s doc says failures are "REPORTED here and swallowed by the afterToolCall wrapper" — but the wrapper (`_attachObligationPendingWaits`) awaits the result and drops it on the floor: nothing is ever reported anywhere, and all the outcome strings (`'pending-wait already recorded…'`, `'did not carry a scheduled id…'`, the swallow-message) are dead text. As written, a silent permanent failure (e.g. the schedule_message result wording changes — see the regex coupling note) is indistinguishable from success.

Either log the outcome through the CLI's logger/bus inside the wrapper, or drop the return value and simplify `recordPendingWait` to `Future<void>` so the code says what it does.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment09.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: only the `result cap` stop carries a continuation token — time-budget stops cannot be paged**

`nextContinuation` is set exclusively when `_stopReason == 'result cap'`. A scan stopped by the 10 s budget mid-archive gets `truncated: true` with no token, so the model's only recourse is the footer advice to narrow with `kinds`/`before`/`after` — fine for specific queries, but for a broad recall sweep over a multi-GB chain there may be no narrowing that fits the budget, and the agent is stuck re-scanning from the start each call (where it will time out again at roughly the same place, since the skip only honors the token).

Since `_skipped` already implements absolute-record skipping, the token is computable for any clean stop: consider `nextContinuation = recordsTotal - 1` (or `recordsTotal`, boundary semantics permitting) whenever the stop was not an error, and extend the footer to offer continuation for `time budget` too.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment11.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "no session file" degradation renders as "no records match" — the graceful-null contract is dishonest in practice**

When the host has no backing session file, this returns `truncated: false, truncationReason: 'no session file'` with zero totals. But `formatSessionSearchOutcome` only surfaces `truncationReason` when `truncated` is true, so the model actually sees:

```text

That claims the archive was scanned and is empty — the opposite of "this host cannot search". The tool-level null-callback branch (`'This host has no session file to search.'`) is never reached from the CLI because the callback is always `searchSessionArchive`. {"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the hit cap is counted before the branch-scope filter — the default scope under-delivers and pages O(n²)**

`seeRecord` stops at `query.maxHits` hits in `_hits`, but `finish()` only then filters to the active branch. Since `branch` is the **default** scope, every match on an abandoned fork consumes budget and can trigger a premature `result cap` that returns far fewer than 40 branch hits — or zero — while reporting `truncated: true`. Worse, the continuation token skips records globally, so each next page re-scans the entire prefix of the chain: paging through a fork-heavy giant session is O(n²) under a 10 s budget.

No test covers branch-scope + cap together (the seeded fork record doesn't match the test query, so the E4 test can't see this).

Directions: collect hits with branch membership decided at collection time where possible, or over-collect with slack and continue scanning when the branch-filtered count is below the cap; alternatively exclude non-branch hits from the cap accounting and document that a capped branch scan may re-examine fork hits on the next page.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment06.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the E5 "never a hang" guarantee is not enforceable — one record can blow the wall-clock budget**

The comment frames this cap as the E5 DoS bound, but a text-length cap is not a time bound on a backtracking regex engine (the Dart VM's `RegExp` backtracks — catastrophic patterns like `(a+)+$` over the 128 KB record are effectively unbounded). The time-budget check (`checkDeadline`) only runs **between** lines/blocks, never inside `pattern.hasMatch`, so a single pathological match on one giant record wedges the tool call — and the cancel token is not consulted during `execute` either — far beyond the promised 10 s, producing a hung agent rather than an "honest `truncated` report".

This matters more here than for a plain grep tool because the regex comes from the model itself, which routinely emits accidentally-quadratic patterns, and this PR's headline scenario is giant records.

Directions: bound the regex subject far smaller (a match over the first N KB of the record's preview-sized excerpt is enough for a pointer), or run the match in an isolate that can be abandoned on deadline expiry, or explicitly scope the E5 claim down to "budget checked between records" and cap per-record regex input accordingly.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment07.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: accumulator state grows linearly with archive size — the flat-memory claim (E4) does not hold**

`scanSessionSegment`'s doc claims "memory stays flat regardless of file size (E4)", and that is true only for the block/carry streaming. The accumulator itself retains per-record state for the whole chain: `_parentOf` for **every** record id (plus `_ordinalOf` in map mode, doubling it). For a multi-GB archive — this PR's explicit target — with a few million records this is hundreds of MB of id→parent pairs held for the entire scan, and it also accumulates identically on every continuation page.

Directions: the branch walk only needs parents of records on the leaf→root path. Since `RangedReadFileSystem` supports ranged reads, consider a two-pass approach (find the leaf in pass 1 storing only checkpoint/parent facts sparsely, then walk backwards in ranges), or keep parents only for records at/after the last observed fork, or correct the doc comment to state the linear bound honestly and decide whether it is acceptable for the E4 giant-session scenario.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment08.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the human-readable outcome of `recordPendingWait` is constructed and then discarded**

`recordPendingWait`'s doc says failures are "REPORTED here and swallowed by the afterToolCall wrapper" — but the wrapper (`_attachObligationPendingWaits`) awaits the result and drops it on the floor: nothing is ever reported anywhere, and all the outcome strings (`'pending-wait already recorded…'`, `'did not carry a scheduled id…'`, the swallow-message) are dead text. As written, a silent permanent failure (e.g. the schedule_message result wording changes — see the regex coupling note) is indistinguishable from success.

Either log the outcome through the CLI's logger/bus inside the wrapper, or drop the return value and simplify `recordPendingWait` to `Future<void>` so the code says what it does.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment09.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: only the `result cap` stop carries a continuation token — time-budget stops cannot be paged**

`nextContinuation` is set exclusively when `_stopReason == 'result cap'`. A scan stopped by the 10 s budget mid-archive gets `truncated: true` with no token, so the model's only recourse is the footer advice to narrow with `kinds`/`before`/`after` — fine for specific queries, but for a broad recall sweep over a multi-GB chain there may be no narrowing that fits the budget, and the agent is stuck re-scanning from the start each call (where it will time out again at roughly the same place, since the skip only honors the token).

Since `_skipped` already implements absolute-record skipping, the token is computable for any clean stop: consider `nextContinuation = recordsTotal - 1` (or `recordsTotal`, boundary semantics permitting) whenever the stop was not an error, and extend the footer to offer continuation for `time budget` too.

","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment02.md"}

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: `recallHygienePrompt` is undefined — the suite fails to load (re-verified on this head)**

This file imports only the public barrel (`package:flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness.dart`), which does **not** export `prompts.g.dart` (the const lives only at `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart:85`). Re-verified locally on head `66f5fc4f0`:

```

```dart

```

Add that import here. Until then the AC6 gate tests — a headline deliverable of this PR — run nowhere.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment03.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "no session file" degradation renders as "no records match" — the graceful-null contract is dishonest in practice**

When the host has no backing session file, this returns `truncated: false, truncationReason: 'no session file'` with zero totals. But `formatSessionSearchOutcome` only surfaces `truncationReason` when `truncated` is true, so the model actually sees:

```text
no records match (examined 0 of 0 records)
```

That claims the archive was scanned and is empty — the opposite of "this host cannot search". The tool-level null-callback branch (`'This host has no session file to search.'`) is never reached from the CLI because the callback is always `searchSessionArchive`. This contradicts the PR's stated "degrades to the same graceful cannot-execute result as ask/request_secret".

Fix options: give `SessionSearchOutcome` a dedicated `unavailableReason` that the formatter prints verbatim, or return `truncated: true` here with the reason (the footer path already prints it). Add a tool-level test that runs the formatter against exactly this outcome.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment05.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the hit cap is counted before the branch-scope filter — the default scope under-delivers and pages O(n²)**

`seeRecord` stops at `query.maxHits` hits in `_hits`, but `finish()` only then filters to the active branch. Since `branch` is the **default** scope, every match on an abandoned fork consumes budget and can trigger a premature `result cap` that returns far fewer than 40 branch hits — or zero — while reporting `truncated: true`. Worse, the continuation token skips records globally, so each next page re-scans the entire prefix of the chain: paging through a fork-heavy giant session is O(n²) under a 10 s budget.

No test covers branch-scope + cap together (the seeded fork record doesn't match the test query, so the E4 test can't see this).

Directions: collect hits with branch membership decided at collection time where possible, or over-collect with slack and continue scanning when the branch-filtered count is below the cap; alternatively exclude non-branch hits from the cap accounting and document that a capped branch scan may re-examine fork hits on the next page.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment06.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the E5 "never a hang" guarantee is not enforceable — one record can blow the wall-clock budget**

The comment frames this cap as the E5 DoS bound, but a text-length cap is not a time bound on a backtracking regex engine (the Dart VM's `RegExp` backtracks — catastrophic patterns like `(a+)+$` over the 128 KB record are effectively unbounded). The time-budget check (`checkDeadline`) only runs **between** lines/blocks, never inside `pattern.hasMatch`, so a single pathological match on one giant record wedges the tool call — and the cancel token is not consulted during `execute` either — far beyond the promised 10 s, producing a hung agent rather than an "honest `truncated` report".

This matters more here than for a plain grep tool because the regex comes from the model itself, which routinely emits accidentally-quadratic patterns, and this PR's headline scenario is giant records.

Directions: bound the regex subject far smaller (a match over the first N KB of the record's preview-sized excerpt is enough for a pointer), or run the match in an isolate that can be abandoned on deadline expiry, or explicitly scope the E5 claim down to "budget checked between records" and cap per-record regex input accordingly.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment07.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: accumulator state grows linearly with archive size — the flat-memory claim (E4) does not hold**

`scanSessionSegment`'s doc claims "memory stays flat regardless of file size (E4)", and that is true only for the block/carry streaming. The accumulator itself retains per-record state for the whole chain: `_parentOf` for **every** record id (plus `_ordinalOf` in map mode, doubling it). For a multi-GB archive — this PR's explicit target — with a few million records this is hundreds of MB of id→parent pairs held for the entire scan, and it also accumulates identically on every continuation page.

Directions: the branch walk only needs parents of records on the leaf→root path. Since `RangedReadFileSystem` supports ranged reads, consider a two-pass approach (find the leaf in pass 1 storing only checkpoint/parent facts sparsely, then walk backwards in ranges), or keep parents only for records at/after the last observed fork, or correct the doc comment to state the linear bound honestly and decide whether it is acceptable for the E4 giant-session scenario.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment08.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the human-readable outcome of `recordPendingWait` is constructed and then discarded**

`recordPendingWait`'s doc says failures are "REPORTED here and swallowed by the afterToolCall wrapper" — but the wrapper (`_attachObligationPendingWaits`) awaits the result and drops it on the floor: nothing is ever reported anywhere, and all the outcome strings (`'pending-wait already recorded…'`, `'did not carry a scheduled id…'`, the swallow-message) are dead text. As written, a silent permanent failure (e.g. the schedule_message result wording changes — see the regex coupling note) is indistinguishable from success.

Either log the outcome through the CLI's logger/bus inside the wrapper, or drop the return value and simplify `recordPendingWait` to `Future<void>` so the code says what it does.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment09.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: only the `result cap` stop carries a continuation token — time-budget stops cannot be paged**

`nextContinuation` is set exclusively when `_stopReason == 'result cap'`. A scan stopped by the 10 s budget mid-archive gets `truncated: true` with no token, so the model's only recourse is the footer advice to narrow with `kinds`/`before`/`after` — fine for specific queries, but for a broad recall sweep over a multi-GB chain there may be no narrowing that fits the budget, and the agent is stuck re-scanning from the start each call (where it will time out again at roughly the same place, since the skip only honors the token).

Since `_skipped` already implements absolute-record skipping, the token is computable for any clean stop: consider `nextContinuation = recordsTotal - 1` (or `recordsTotal`, boundary semantics permitting) whenever the stop was not an error, and extend the footer to offer continuation for `time budget` too.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment11.md"}

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. A. `_hasNestedQuantifier` — hand-rolled regex parser. Look for bugs:

Correct: if group body contains quantified atom → group has quantified body. Yes.
   - But there's a subtle bug: when a group closes, `lastGroupHasQuantified` is set. But if the NEXT char is not a quantifier, lastGroupHasQuantified remains stale... e.g. `(a+)b` — at `)`, lastGroupHasQuantified=true, lastAtomWasGroup=true. At `b` → default: lastAtomWasGroup=false. OK reset.
   - `(a+)+` → `(` push false; `a` default resets; `+` marks group last=true, lastAtomQuantified=true; `)` pops → lastGroupHasQuantified=true, lastAtomWasGroup=true; `+` → lastAtomWasGroup && lastGroupHasQuantified → true. 
   - `(\w+)+` similar.
   - What about `(a+)+?` — lazy modifier: `+` after group → return true at the second `+`. Fine.
   - `((a+))` → inner: group2 has quantified; at first `)` (closing group2) lastGroupHasQuantified=true; second `)` closes group1 — group1's flag: group1 body contains group2 which is quantified inside... groupHasQuantified for group1 was set only when a quantifier directly appeared while group1 was top of stack. The quantifier `+` after `a` appeared while stack top was group2 (both pushed). So group1's flag NOT set. Hmm — is `((a+))+` caught? Parse: `(` push g1=false (i=0). `(` push g2=false (i=1). `a` default (i=2). `+` (i=3): stack top g2 → g2=true; lastAtomQuantified=true. `)` (i=4): pop g2 → lastGroupHasQuantified=true, lastAtomWasGroup=true. `)` (i=5): pop g1 → g1's stored flag = false → lastGroupHasQuantified=false, lastAtomWasGroup=true. `+` (i=6): lastAtomWasGroup && lastGroupHasQuantified → false → NOT detected. So `((a+))+` passes the screen but is catastrophic. False negatives exist. But the doc says ambiguous shapes not screened; nested groups shape... The honest doc says residual is scoped & documented ("one unscreened pathological match ... can still exceed the budget; that residual is scoped, documented"). Still, `((a+))+` is precisely the "(a+)+-shape" the error message names, just wrapped — a model could easily produce it. Is this worth a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? The screen is best-effort with documented residual. False negatives for doubly-nested groups is a reasonable limitation; but since the parse-time rejection is the headline E5 defense, a note could be added. I'd file this as SUGGESTION: propagate the "contains quantified group" fact outward so `((a+))+` is also rejected, or extend the error message. Actually wait — also check `(a*)*` etc. Similar. And what about `(?:a+)+`? `(` at i, pattern[i+1]=='?' → i++ (skips '?'); then `a` default, `+` marks top group true, `)` pops → lastGroupHasQuantified=true, `+` → detected. Good.
   
   Also `case '?'`: `if (lastAtomQuantified) { lastAtomQuantified = false; break; }` — lazy modifier consumed. But what about `??`? first `?`: lastAtomQuantified false (e.g. after `a`)... wait `a??` — `a` default → lastAtomQuantified=false; `?` → not lastAtomQuantified → sets lastAtomQuantified=true, marks group. Second `?` → lastAtomQuantified true → lazy → break. OK.
   
   Backreference `\1` — escaped handling resets atom flags. OK.

   Another subtlety: `{` bounded quantifier on group: `(a+){2}` → at `{`: isQuantifier true; lastAtomWasGroup && lastGroupHasQuantified → return true. Good.

B. Census pass cost: searchSessionFile with branch scope now scans the file TWICE (census + real pass) under the SAME 10s deadline. The deadline is shared (`deadline = now + budget` computed once, passed to both accumulators). So the census consumes part of the budget, then the real pass gets the remainder. On a huge archive, the census pass alone could eat most of the 10s, leaving little for the real scan — meaning the default-scope search on a giant session will routinely time out before finding anything. Is this flagged? The docstring says "Map mode and branch scope pay one extra read-only census pass first". The 10s budget is shared across both passes, which is at least honest about wall clock. But it doubles the I/O+decode cost for the default scope. Trade-off — the alternative (cap fork hits) under-delivers. The time budget covers the total. Hmm — this means the default branch-scope search is now ~2x slower than before per archive byte, and the previous "examine N of M records" semantics... recordsExamined only counts the real pass; census pass doubles actual work but reports examined from real pass. The model sees "examined 500 of 100" while wall clock burned 2x. Acceptable; documented? Not explicitly. Could be a SUGGESTION: consider whether the census should get its own sub-budget or be skipped under continuation (on page 2+, the census re-runs again! Every continuation page re-scans the whole chain for the census AND the real pass — so page n costs (n+1) full-prefix scans... wait: continuation skips records in the real pass via _skipped, but the scan still reads/decodes every line from the start (seeLine → seeRecord increments recordsTotal and checks _skipped). And the census pass re-runs completely on every page (no continuation skip in census — census.seeRecord doesn't handle query.continuation... it counts recordsTotal and returns; no skip logic. So the census scans the entire chain every page). So paging a giant session is O(pages × full chain) — for page 10 of a 1GB archive that's 10 full reads. Previously it was also re-reading the prefix (the O(n²) note in thread 6 mentioned continuation token skips records globally so each page re-scans the entire prefix). So paging behavior unchanged in asymptotic terms; the census adds a constant 2x per page. The thread 6 finding's O(n²) concern was about paging re-scanning prefix — still true but that was deemed acceptable? The finding said paging is O(n²) under a 10s budget; the fix addresses the cap-under-delivery, not the O(n²) paging. The continuation skip is logical (not I/O), so re-reading is inherent to index-free v1 (Q3: index-free stands). OK.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "no session file" degradation renders as "no records match" — the graceful-null contract is dishonest in practice**

When the host has no backing session file, this returns `truncated: false, truncationReason: 'no session file'` with zero totals. But `formatSessionSearchOutcome` only surfaces `truncationReason` when `truncated` is true, so the model actually sees:

```text

```

That claims the archive was scanned and is empty — the opposite of "this host cannot search". The tool-level null-callback branch (`'This host has no session file to search.'`) is never reached from the CLI because the callback is always `searchSessionArchive`. {"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the hit cap is counted before the branch-scope filter — the default scope under-delivers and pages O(n²)**

`seeRecord` stops at `query.maxHits` hits in `_hits`, but `finish()` only then filters to the active branch. Since `branch` is the **default** scope, every match on an abandoned fork consumes budget and can trigger a premature `result cap` that returns far fewer than 40 branch hits — or zero — while reporting `truncated: true`. Worse, the continuation token skips records globally, so each next page re-scans the entire prefix of the chain: paging through a fork-heavy giant session is O(n²) under a 10 s budget.

No test covers branch-scope + cap together (the seeded fork record doesn't match the test query, so the E4 test can't see this).

Directions: collect hits with branch membership decided at collection time where possible, or over-collect with slack and continue scanning when the branch-filtered count is below the cap; alternatively exclude non-branch hits from the cap accounting and document that a capped branch scan may re-examine fork hits on the next page.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment06.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the E5 "never a hang" guarantee is not enforceable — one record can blow the wall-clock budget**

The comment frames this cap as the E5 DoS bound, but a text-length cap is not a time bound on a backtracking regex engine (the Dart VM's `RegExp` backtracks — catastrophic patterns like `(a+)+$` over the 128 KB record are effectively unbounded). The time-budget check (`checkDeadline`) only runs **between** lines/blocks, never inside `pattern.hasMatch`, so a single pathological match on one giant record wedges the tool call — and the cancel token is not consulted during `execute` either — far beyond the promised 10 s, producing a hung agent rather than an "honest `truncated` report".

This matters more here than for a plain grep tool because the regex comes from the model itself, which routinely emits accidentally-quadratic patterns, and this PR's headline scenario is giant records.

Directions: bound the regex subject far smaller (a match over the first N KB of the record's preview-sized excerpt is enough for a pointer), or run the match in an isolate that can be abandoned on deadline expiry, or explicitly scope the E5 claim down to "budget checked between records" and cap per-record regex input accordingly.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment07.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: accumulator state grows linearly with archive size — the flat-memory claim (E4) does not hold**

`scanSessionSegment`'s doc claims "memory stays flat regardless of file size (E4)", and that is true only for the block/carry streaming. The accumulator itself retains per-record state for the whole chain: `_parentOf` for **every** record id (plus `_ordinalOf` in map mode, doubling it). For a multi-GB archive — this PR's explicit target — with a few million records this is hundreds of MB of id→parent pairs held for the entire scan, and it also accumulates identically on every continuation page.

Directions: the branch walk only needs parents of records on the leaf→root path. Since `RangedReadFileSystem` supports ranged reads, consider a two-pass approach (find the leaf in pass 1 storing only checkpoint/parent facts sparsely, then walk backwards in ranges), or keep parents only for records at/after the last observed fork, or correct the doc comment to state the linear bound honestly and decide whether it is acceptable for the E4 giant-session scenario.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment08.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: only the `result cap` stop carries a continuation token — time-budget stops cannot be paged**

`nextContinuation` is set exclusively when `_stopReason == 'result cap'`. A scan stopped by the 10 s budget mid-archive gets `truncated: true` with no token, so the model's only recourse is the footer advice to narrow with `kinds`/`before`/`after` — fine for specific queries, but for a broad recall sweep over a multi-GB chain there may be no narrowing that fits the budget, and the agent is stuck re-scanning from the start each call (where it will time out again at roughly the same place, since the skip only honors the token).

Since `_skipped` already implements absolute-record skipping, the token is computable for any clean stop: consider `nextContinuation = recordsTotal - 1` (or `recordsTotal`, boundary semantics permitting) whenever the stop was not an error, and extend the footer to offer continuation for `time budget` too.

Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. {"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: `recallHygienePrompt` is undefined — the suite fails to load (re-verified on this head)**

This file imports only the public barrel (`package:flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness.dart`), which does **not** export `prompts.g.dart` (the const lives only at `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart:85`). Re-verified locally on head `66f5fc4f0`:

","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment03.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "no session file" degradation renders as "no records match" — the graceful-null contract is dishonest in practice**

When the host has no backing session file, this returns `truncated: false, truncationReason: 'no session file'` with zero totals. But `formatSessionSearchOutcome` only surfaces `truncationReason` when `truncated` is true, so the model actually sees:

```text
no records match (examined 0 of 0 records)
```

That claims the archive was scanned and is empty — the opposite of "this host cannot search". The tool-level null-callback branch (`'This host has no session file to search.'`) is never reached from the CLI because the callback is always `searchSessionArchive`. This contradicts the PR's stated "degrades to the same graceful cannot-execute result as ask/request_secret".

Fix options: give `SessionSearchOutcome` a dedicated `unavailableReason` that the formatter prints verbatim, or return `truncated: true` here with the reason (the footer path already prints it). Add a tool-level test that runs the formatter against exactly this outcome.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment05.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the hit cap is counted before the branch-scope filter — the default scope under-delivers and pages O(n²)**

`seeRecord` stops at `query.maxHits` hits in `_hits`, but `finish()` only then filters to the active branch. Since `branch` is the **default** scope, every match on an abandoned fork consumes budget and can trigger a premature `result cap` that returns far fewer than 40 branch hits — or zero — while reporting `truncated: true`. Worse, the continuation token skips records globally, so each next page re-scans the entire prefix of the chain: paging through a fork-heavy giant session is O(n²) under a 10 s budget.

No test covers branch-scope + cap together (the seeded fork record doesn't match the test query, so the E4 test can't see this).

Directions: collect hits with branch membership decided at collection time where possible, or over-collect with slack and continue scanning when the branch-filtered count is below the cap; alternatively exclude non-branch hits from the cap accounting and document that a capped branch scan may re-examine fork hits on the next page.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment06.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the E5 "never a hang" guarantee is not enforceable — one record can blow the wall-clock budget**

The comment frames this cap as the E5 DoS bound, but a text-length cap is not a time bound on a backtracking regex engine (the Dart VM's `RegExp` backtracks — catastrophic patterns like `(a+)+$` over the 128 KB record are effectively unbounded). The time-budget check (`checkDeadline`) only runs **between** lines/blocks, never inside `pattern.hasMatch`, so a single pathological match on one giant record wedges the tool call — and the cancel token is not consulted during `execute` either — far beyond the promised 10 s, producing a hung agent rather than an "honest `truncated` report".

This matters more here than for a plain grep tool because the regex comes from the model itself, which routinely emits accidentally-quadratic patterns, and this PR's headline scenario is giant records.

Directions: bound the regex subject far smaller (a match over the first N KB of the record's preview-sized excerpt is enough for a pointer), or run the match in an isolate that can be abandoned on deadline expiry, or explicitly scope the E5 claim down to "budget checked between records" and cap per-record regex input accordingly.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment07.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: accumulator state grows linearly with archive size — the flat-memory claim (E4) does not hold**

`scanSessionSegment`'s doc claims "memory stays flat regardless of file size (E4)", and that is true only for the block/carry streaming. The accumulator itself retains per-record state for the whole chain: `_parentOf` for **every** record id (plus `_ordinalOf` in map mode, doubling it). For a multi-GB archive — this PR's explicit target — with a few million records this is hundreds of MB of id→parent pairs held for the entire scan, and it also accumulates identically on every continuation page.

Directions: the branch walk only needs parents of records on the leaf→root path. Since `RangedReadFileSystem` supports ranged reads, consider a two-pass approach (find the leaf in pass 1 storing only checkpoint/parent facts sparsely, then walk backwards in ranges), or keep parents only for records at/after the last observed fork, or correct the doc comment to state the linear bound honestly and decide whether it is acceptable for the E4 giant-session scenario.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment08.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the human-readable outcome of `recordPendingWait` is constructed and then discarded**

`recordPendingWait`'s doc says failures are "REPORTED here and swallowed by the afterToolCall wrapper" — but the wrapper (`_attachObligationPendingWaits`) awaits the result and drops it on the floor: nothing is ever reported anywhere, and all the outcome strings (`'pending-wait already recorded…'`, `'did not carry a scheduled id…'`, the swallow-message) are dead text. As written, a silent permanent failure (e.g. the schedule_message result wording changes — see the regex coupling note) is indistinguishable from success.

Either log the outcome through the CLI's logger/bus inside the wrapper, or drop the return value and simplify `recordPendingWait` to `Future<void>` so the code says what it does.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment09.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: only the `result cap` stop carries a continuation token — time-budget stops cannot be paged**

`nextContinuation` is set exclusively when `_stopReason == 'result cap'`. A scan stopped by the 10 s budget mid-archive gets `truncated: true` with no token, so the model's only recourse is the footer advice to narrow with `kinds`/`before`/`after` — fine for specific queries, but for a broad recall sweep over a multi-GB chain there may be no narrowing that fits the budget, and the agent is stuck re-scanning from the start each call (where it will time out again at roughly the same place, since the skip only honors the token).

Since `_skipped` already implements absolute-record skipping, the token is computable for any clean stop: consider `nextContinuation = recordsTotal - 1` (or `recordsTotal`, boundary semantics permitting) whenever the stop was not an error, and extend the footer to offer continuation for `time budget` too.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment11.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "no session file" degradation renders as "no records match" — the graceful-null contract is dishonest in practice**

When the host has no backing session file, this returns `truncated: false, truncationReason: 'no session file'` with zero totals. But `formatSessionSearchOutcome` only surfaces `truncationReason` when `truncated` is true, so the model actually sees:

```text
no records match (examined 0 of 0 records)
```

That claims the archive was scanned and is empty — the opposite of "this host cannot search". The tool-level null-callback branch (`'This host has no session file to search.'`) is never reached from the CLI because the callback is always `searchSessionArchive`. This contradicts the PR's stated "degrades to the same graceful cannot-execute result as ask/request_secret".

Fix options: give `SessionSearchOutcome` a dedicated `unavailableReason` that the formatter prints verbatim, or return `truncated: true` here with the reason (the footer path already prints it). Add a tool-level test that runs the formatter against exactly this outcome.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment05.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the hit cap is counted before the branch-scope filter — the default scope under-delivers and pages O(n²)**

`seeRecord` stops at `query.maxHits` hits in `_hits`, but `finish()` only then filters to the active branch. Since `branch` is the **default** scope, every match on an abandoned fork consumes budget and can trigger a premature `result cap` that returns far fewer than 40 branch hits — or zero — while reporting `truncated: true`. Worse, the continuation token skips records globally, so each next page re-scans the entire prefix of the chain: paging through a fork-heavy giant session is O(n²) under a 10 s budget.

No test covers branch-scope + cap together (the seeded fork record doesn't match the test query, so the E4 test can't see this).

Directions: collect hits with branch membership decided at collection time where possible, or over-collect with slack and continue scanning when the branch-filtered count is below the cap; alternatively exclude non-branch hits from the cap accounting and document that a capped branch scan may re-examine fork hits on the next page.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment06.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the E5 "never a hang" guarantee is not enforceable — one record can blow the wall-clock budget**

The comment frames this cap as the E5 DoS bound, but a text-length cap is not a time bound on a backtracking regex engine (the Dart VM's `RegExp` backtracks — catastrophic patterns like `(a+)+$` over the 128 KB record are effectively unbounded). The time-budget check (`checkDeadline`) only runs **between** lines/blocks, never inside `pattern.hasMatch`, so a single pathological match on one giant record wedges the tool call — and the cancel token is not consulted during `execute` either — far beyond the promised 10 s, producing a hung agent rather than an "honest `truncated` report".

This matters more here than for a plain grep tool because the regex comes from the model itself, which routinely emits accidentally-quadratic patterns, and this PR's headline scenario is giant records.

Directions: bound the regex subject far smaller (a match over the first N KB of the record's preview-sized excerpt is enough for a pointer), or run the match in an isolate that can be abandoned on deadline expiry, or explicitly scope the E5 claim down to "budget checked between records" and cap per-record regex input accordingly.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment07.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: accumulator state grows linearly with archive size — the flat-memory claim (E4) does not hold**

`scanSessionSegment`'s doc claims "memory stays flat regardless of file size (E4)", and that is true only for the block/carry streaming. The accumulator itself retains per-record state for the whole chain: `_parentOf` for **every** record id (plus `_ordinalOf` in map mode, doubling it). For a multi-GB archive — this PR's explicit target — with a few million records this is hundreds of MB of id→parent pairs held for the entire scan, and it also accumulates identically on every continuation page.

Directions: the branch walk only needs parents of records on the leaf→root path. Since `RangedReadFileSystem` supports ranged reads, consider a two-pass approach (find the leaf in pass 1 storing only checkpoint/parent facts sparsely, then walk backwards in ranges), or keep parents only for records at/after the last observed fork, or correct the doc comment to state the linear bound honestly and decide whether it is acceptable for the E4 giant-session scenario.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment08.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the human-readable outcome of `recordPendingWait` is constructed and then discarded**

`recordPendingWait`'s doc says failures are "REPORTED here and swallowed by the afterToolCall wrapper" — but the wrapper (`_attachObligationPendingWaits`) awaits the result and drops it on the floor: nothing is ever reported anywhere, and all the outcome strings (`'pending-wait already recorded…'`, `'did not carry a scheduled id…'`, the swallow-message) are dead text. As written, a silent permanent failure (e.g. the schedule_message result wording changes — see the regex coupling note) is indistinguishable from success.

Either log the outcome through the CLI's logger/bus inside the wrapper, or drop the return value and simplify `recordPendingWait` to `Future<void>` so the code says what it does.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment09.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: only the `result cap` stop carries a continuation token — time-budget stops cannot be paged**

`nextContinuation` is set exclusively when `_stopReason == 'result cap'`. A scan stopped by the 10 s budget mid-archive gets `truncated: true` with no token, so the model's only recourse is the footer advice to narrow with `kinds`/`before`/`after` — fine for specific queries, but for a broad recall sweep over a multi-GB chain there may be no narrowing that fits the budget, and the agent is stuck re-scanning from the start each call (where it will time out again at roughly the same place, since the skip only honors the token).

Since `_skipped` already implements absolute-record skipping, the token is computable for any clean stop: consider `nextContinuation = recordsTotal - 1` (or `recordsTotal`, boundary semantics permitting) whenever the stop was not an error, and extend the footer to offer continuation for `time budget` too.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment11.md"}

Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. ","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment02.md"}

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: `recallHygienePrompt` is undefined — the suite fails to load (re-verified on this head)**

This file imports only the public barrel (`package:flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness.dart`), which does **not** export `prompts.g.dart` (the const lives only at `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart:85`). Re-verified locally on head `66f5fc4f0`:

```

```

Add that import here. Until then the AC6 gate tests — a headline deliverable of this PR — run nowhere.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment03.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "no session file" degradation renders as "no records match" — the graceful-null contract is dishonest in practice**

When the host has no backing session file, this returns `truncated: false, truncationReason: 'no session file'` with zero totals. But `formatSessionSearchOutcome` only surfaces `truncationReason` when `truncated` is true, so the model actually sees:

```text
no records match (examined 0 of 0 records)
```

That claims the archive was scanned and is empty — the opposite of "this host cannot search". The tool-level null-callback branch (`'This host has no session file to search.'`) is never reached from the CLI because the callback is always `searchSessionArchive`. This contradicts the PR's stated "degrades to the same graceful cannot-execute result as ask/request_secret".

Fix options: give `SessionSearchOutcome` a dedicated `unavailableReason` that the formatter prints verbatim, or return `truncated: true` here with the reason (the footer path already prints it). Add a tool-level test that runs the formatter against exactly this outcome.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment05.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the hit cap is counted before the branch-scope filter — the default scope under-delivers and pages O(n²)**

`seeRecord` stops at `query.maxHits` hits in `_hits`, but `finish()` only then filters to the active branch. Since `branch` is the **default** scope, every match on an abandoned fork consumes budget and can trigger a premature `result cap` that returns far fewer than 40 branch hits — or zero — while reporting `truncated: true`. Worse, the continuation token skips records globally, so each next page re-scans the entire prefix of the chain: paging through a fork-heavy giant session is O(n²) under a 10 s budget.

No test covers branch-scope + cap together (the seeded fork record doesn't match the test query, so the E4 test can't see this).

Directions: collect hits with branch membership decided at collection time where possible, or over-collect with slack and continue scanning when the branch-filtered count is below the cap; alternatively exclude non-branch hits from the cap accounting and document that a capped branch scan may re-examine fork hits on the next page.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment06.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the E5 "never a hang" guarantee is not enforceable — one record can blow the wall-clock budget**

The comment frames this cap as the E5 DoS bound, but a text-length cap is not a time bound on a backtracking regex engine (the Dart VM's `RegExp` backtracks — catastrophic patterns like `(a+)+$` over the 128 KB record are effectively unbounded). The time-budget check (`checkDeadline`) only runs **between** lines/blocks, never inside `pattern.hasMatch`, so a single pathological match on one giant record wedges the tool call — and the cancel token is not consulted during `execute` either — far beyond the promised 10 s, producing a hung agent rather than an "honest `truncated` report".

This matters more here than for a plain grep tool because the regex comes from the model itself, which routinely emits accidentally-quadratic patterns, and this PR's headline scenario is giant records.

Directions: bound the regex subject far smaller (a match over the first N KB of the record's preview-sized excerpt is enough for a pointer), or run the match in an isolate that can be abandoned on deadline expiry, or explicitly scope the E5 claim down to "budget checked between records" and cap per-record regex input accordingly.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment07.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: accumulator state grows linearly with archive size — the flat-memory claim (E4) does not hold**

`scanSessionSegment`'s doc claims "memory stays flat regardless of file size (E4)", and that is true only for the block/carry streaming. The accumulator itself retains per-record state for the whole chain: `_parentOf` for **every** record id (plus `_ordinalOf` in map mode, doubling it). For a multi-GB archive — this PR's explicit target — with a few million records this is hundreds of MB of id→parent pairs held for the entire scan, and it also accumulates identically on every continuation page.

Directions: the branch walk only needs parents of records on the leaf→root path. Since `RangedReadFileSystem` supports ranged reads, consider a two-pass approach (find the leaf in pass 1 storing only checkpoint/parent facts sparsely, then walk backwards in ranges), or keep parents only for records at/after the last observed fork, or correct the doc comment to state the linear bound honestly and decide whether it is acceptable for the E4 giant-session scenario.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment08.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the human-readable outcome of `recordPendingWait` is constructed and then discarded**

`recordPendingWait`'s doc says failures are "REPORTED here and swallowed by the afterToolCall wrapper" — but the wrapper (`_attachObligationPendingWaits`) awaits the result and drops it on the floor: nothing is ever reported anywhere, and all the outcome strings (`'pending-wait already recorded…'`, `'did not carry a scheduled id…'`, the swallow-message) are dead text. As written, a silent permanent failure (e.g. the schedule_message result wording changes — see the regex coupling note) is indistinguishable from success.

Either log the outcome through the CLI's logger/bus inside the wrapper, or drop the return value and simplify `recordPendingWait` to `Future<void>` so the code says what it does.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment09.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: only the `result cap` stop carries a continuation token — time-budget stops cannot be paged**

`nextContinuation` is set exclusively when `_stopReason == 'result cap'`. A scan stopped by the 10 s budget mid-archive gets `truncated: true` with no token, so the model's only recourse is the footer advice to narrow with `kinds`/`before`/`after` — fine for specific queries, but for a broad recall sweep over a multi-GB chain there may be no narrowing that fits the budget, and the agent is stuck re-scanning from the start each call (where it will time out again at roughly the same place, since the skip only honors the token).

Since `_skipped` already implements absolute-record skipping, the token is computable for any clean stop: consider `nextContinuation = recordsTotal - 1` (or `recordsTotal`, boundary semantics permitting) whenever the stop was not an error, and extend the footer to offer continuation for `time budget` too.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment11.md"}

The time-budget check (`checkDeadline`) only runs **between** lines/blocks, never inside `pattern.hasMatch`, so a single pathological match on one giant record wedges the tool call — and the cancel token is not consulted during `execute` either — far beyond the promised 10 s, producing a hung agent rather than an "honest `truncated` report".

This matters more here than for a plain grep tool because the regex comes from the model itself, which routinely emits accidentally-quadratic patterns, and this PR's headline scenario is giant records.

Directions: bound the regex subject far smaller (a match over the first N KB of the record's preview-sized excerpt is enough for a pointer), or run the match in an isolate that can be abandoned on deadline expiry, or explicitly scope the E5 claim down to "budget checked between records" and cap per-record regex input accordingly.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment07.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: accumulator state grows linearly with archive size — the flat-memory claim (E4) does not hold**

`scanSessionSegment`'s doc claims "memory stays flat regardless of file size (E4)", and that is true only for the block/carry streaming. The accumulator itself retains per-record state for the whole chain: `_parentOf` for **every** record id (plus `_ordinalOf` in map mode, doubling it). For a multi-GB archive — this PR's explicit target — with a few million records this is hundreds of MB of id→parent pairs held for the entire scan, and it also accumulates identically on every continuation page.

Directions: the branch walk only needs parents of records on the leaf→root path. Since `RangedReadFileSystem` supports ranged reads, consider a two-pass approach (find the leaf in pass 1 storing only checkpoint/parent facts sparsely, then walk backwards in ranges), or keep parents only for records at/after the last observed fork, or correct the doc comment to state the linear bound honestly and decide whether it is acceptable for the E4 giant-session scenario.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment08.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the human-readable outcome of `recordPendingWait` is constructed and then discarded**

`recordPendingWait`'s doc says failures are "REPORTED here and swallowed by the afterToolCall wrapper" — but the wrapper (`_attachObligationPendingWaits`) awaits the result and drops it on the floor: nothing is ever reported anywhere, and all the outcome strings (`'pending-wait already recorded…'`, `'did not carry a scheduled id…'`, the swallow-message) are dead text. As written, a silent permanent failure (e.g. the schedule_message result wording changes — see the regex coupling note) is indistinguishable from success.

Either log the outcome through the CLI's logger/bus inside the wrapper, or drop the return value and simplify `recordPendingWait` to `Future<void>` so the code says what it does.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment09.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: only the `result cap` stop carries a continuation token — time-budget stops cannot be paged**

`nextContinuation` is set exclusively when `_stopReason == 'result cap'`. A scan stopped by the 10 s budget mid-archive gets `truncated: true` with no token, so the model's only recourse is the footer advice to narrow with `kinds`/`before`/`after` — fine for specific queries, but for a broad recall sweep over a multi-GB chain there may be no narrowing that fits the budget, and the agent is stuck re-scanning from the start each call (where it will time out again at roughly the same place, since the skip only honors the token).

Since `_skipped` already implements absolute-record skipping, the token is computable for any clean stop: consider `nextContinuation = recordsTotal - 1` (or `recordsTotal`, boundary semantics permitting) whenever the stop was not an error, and extend the footer to offer continuation for `time budget` too.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "no session file" degradation renders as "no records match" — the graceful-null contract is dishonest in practice**

When the host has no backing session file, this returns `truncated: false, truncationReason: 'no session file'` with zero totals. But `formatSessionSearchOutcome` only surfaces `truncationReason` when `truncated` is true, so the model actually sees:

```text
no records match (examined 0 of 0 records)
```

That claims the archive was scanned and is empty — the opposite of "this host cannot search". The tool-level null-callback branch (`'This host has no session file to search.'`) is never reached from the CLI because the callback is always `searchSessionArchive`. This contradicts the PR's stated "degrades to the same graceful cannot-execute result as ask/request_secret".

Fix options: give `SessionSearchOutcome` a dedicated `unavailableReason` that the formatter prints verbatim, or return `truncated: true` here with the reason (the footer path already prints it). Add a tool-level test that runs the formatter against exactly this outcome.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment05.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the hit cap is counted before the branch-scope filter — the default scope under-delivers and pages O(n²)**

`seeRecord` stops at `query.maxHits` hits in `_hits`, but `finish()` only then filters to the active branch. Since `branch` is the **default** scope, every match on an abandoned fork consumes budget and can trigger a premature `result cap` that returns far fewer than 40 branch hits — or zero — while reporting `truncated: true`. Worse, the continuation token skips records globally, so each next page re-scans the entire prefix of the chain: paging through a fork-heavy giant session is O(n²) under a 10 s budget.

No test covers branch-scope + cap together (the seeded fork record doesn't match the test query, so the E4 test can't see this).

Directions: collect hits with branch membership decided at collection time where possible, or over-collect with slack and continue scanning when the branch-filtered count is below the cap; alternatively exclude non-branch hits from the cap accounting and document that a capped branch scan may re-examine fork hits on the next page.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment06.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the E5 "never a hang" guarantee is not enforceable — one record can blow the wall-clock budget**

The comment frames this cap as the E5 DoS bound, but a text-length cap is not a time bound on a backtracking regex engine (the Dart VM's `RegExp` backtracks — catastrophic patterns like `(a+)+$` over the 128 KB record are effectively unbounded). The time-budget check (`checkDeadline`) only runs **between** lines/blocks, never inside `pattern.hasMatch`, so a single pathological match on one giant record wedges the tool call — and the cancel token is not consulted during `execute` either — far beyond the promised 10 s, producing a hung agent rather than an "honest `truncated` report".

This matters more here than for a plain grep tool because the regex comes from the model itself, which routinely emits accidentally-quadratic patterns, and this PR's headline scenario is giant records.

Directions: bound the regex subject far smaller (a match over the first N KB of the record's preview-sized excerpt is enough for a pointer), or run the match in an isolate that can be abandoned on deadline expiry, or explicitly scope the E5 claim down to "budget checked between records" and cap per-record regex input accordingly.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment07.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: accumulator state grows linearly with archive size — the flat-memory claim (E4) does not hold**

`scanSessionSegment`'s doc claims "memory stays flat regardless of file size (E4)", and that is true only for the block/carry streaming. The accumulator itself retains per-record state for the whole chain: `_parentOf` for **every** record id (plus `_ordinalOf` in map mode, doubling it). For a multi-GB archive — this PR's explicit target — with a few million records this is hundreds of MB of id→parent pairs held for the entire scan, and it also accumulates identically on every continuation page.

Directions: the branch walk only needs parents of records on the leaf→root path. Since `RangedReadFileSystem` supports ranged reads, consider a two-pass approach (find the leaf in pass 1 storing only checkpoint/parent facts sparsely, then walk backwards in ranges), or keep parents only for records at/after the last observed fork, or correct the doc comment to state the linear bound honestly and decide whether it is acceptable for the E4 giant-session scenario.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment08.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the human-readable outcome of `recordPendingWait` is constructed and then discarded**

`recordPendingWait`'s doc says failures are "REPORTED here and swallowed by the afterToolCall wrapper" — but the wrapper (`_attachObligationPendingWaits`) awaits the result and drops it on the floor: nothing is ever reported anywhere, and all the outcome strings (`'pending-wait already recorded…'`, `'did not carry a scheduled id…'`, the swallow-message) are dead text. As written, a silent permanent failure (e.g. the schedule_message result wording changes — see the regex coupling note) is indistinguishable from success.

Either log the outcome through the CLI's logger/bus inside the wrapper, or drop the return value and simplify `recordPendingWait` to `Future<void>` so the code says what it does.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment09.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: only the `result cap` stop carries a continuation token — time-budget stops cannot be paged**

`nextContinuation` is set exclusively when `_stopReason == 'result cap'`. A scan stopped by the 10 s budget mid-archive gets `truncated: true` with no token, so the model's only recourse is the footer advice to narrow with `kinds`/`before`/`after` — fine for specific queries, but for a broad recall sweep over a multi-GB chain there may be no narrowing that fits the budget, and the agent is stuck re-scanning from the start each call (where it will time out again at roughly the same place, since the skip only honors the token).

Since `_skipped` already implements absolute-record skipping, the token is computable for any clean stop: consider `nextContinuation = recordsTotal - 1` (or `recordsTotal`, boundary semantics permitting) whenever the stop was not an error, and extend the footer to offer continuation for `time budget` too.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment11.md"}

13. Cross-tool contract comment — schedule_message_tool.dart +5 lines; check.

Now the exhaustive pass for NEW issues in the rework. Things to scrutinize:

A. `_hasNestedQuantifier` — hand-rolled regex parser. Look for bugs:
   - `case '+': if (lastAtomWasGroup && lastGroupHasQuantified) return true; lastAtomQuantified = true; if (groupHasQuantified.isNotEmpty) groupHasQuantified.last = true;` — hmm, this marks the CURRENT group's body as having a quantified atom whenever ANY atom is quantified. Correct: if group body contains quantified atom → group has quantified body. Yes.
   - But there's a subtle bug: when a group closes, `lastGroupHasQuantified` is set. But if the NEXT char is not a quantifier, lastGroupHasQuantified remains stale... e.g. `(a+)b` — at `)`, lastGroupHasQuantified=true, lastAtomWasGroup=true. At `b` → default: lastAtomWasGroup=false. OK reset.
   - `(a+)+` → `(` push false; `a` default resets; `+` marks group last=true, lastAtomQuantified=true; `)` pops → lastGroupHasQuantified=true, lastAtomWasGroup=true; `+` → lastAtomWasGroup && lastGroupHasQuantified → true. 
   - `(\w+)+` similar.
   - What about `(a+)+?` — lazy modifier: `+` after group → return true at the second `+`. Fine.
   - `((a+))` → inner: group2 has quantified; at first `)` (closing group2) lastGroupHasQuantified=true; second `)` closes group1 — group1's flag: group1 body contains group2 which is quantified inside... groupHasQuantified for group1 was set only when a quantifier directly appeared while group1 was top of stack. The quantifier `+` after `a` appeared while stack top was group2 (both pushed). So group1's flag NOT set. Hmm — is `((a+))+` caught? Parse: `(` push g1=false (i=0). `(` push g2=false (i=1). `a` default (i=2). `+` (i=3): stack top g2 → g2=true; lastAtomQuantified=true. `)` (i=4): pop g2 → lastGroupHasQuantified=true, lastAtomWasGroup=true. `)` (i=5): pop g1 → g1's stored flag = false → lastGroupHasQuantified=false, lastAtomWasGroup=true. `+` (i=6): lastAtomWasGroup && lastGroupHasQuantified → false → NOT detected. {"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "no session file" degradation renders as "no records match" — the graceful-null contract is dishonest in practice**

When the host has no backing session file, this returns `truncated: false, truncationReason: 'no session file'` with zero totals. But `formatSessionSearchOutcome` only surfaces `truncationReason` when `truncated` is true, so the model actually sees:

```text
no records match (examined 0 of 0 records)
```

That claims the archive was scanned and is empty — the opposite of "this host cannot search". The tool-level null-callback branch (`'This host has no session file to search.'`) is never reached from the CLI because the callback is always `searchSessionArchive`. This contradicts the PR's stated "degrades to the same graceful cannot-execute result as ask/request_secret".

Fix options: give `SessionSearchOutcome` a dedicated `unavailableReason` that the formatter prints verbatim, or return `truncated: true` here with the reason (the footer path already prints it). Add a tool-level test that runs the formatter against exactly this outcome.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment05.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the hit cap is counted before the branch-scope filter — the default scope under-delivers and pages O(n²)**

`seeRecord` stops at `query.maxHits` hits in `_hits`, but `finish()` only then filters to the active branch. Since `branch` is the **default** scope, every match on an abandoned fork consumes budget and can trigger a premature `result cap` that returns far fewer than 40 branch hits — or zero — while reporting `truncated: true`. Worse, the continuation token skips records globally, so each next page re-scans the entire prefix of the chain: paging through a fork-heavy giant session is O(n²) under a 10 s budget.

No test covers branch-scope + cap together (the seeded fork record doesn't match the test query, so the E4 test can't see this).

Directions: collect hits with branch membership decided at collection time where possible, or over-collect with slack and continue scanning when the branch-filtered count is below the cap; alternatively exclude non-branch hits from the cap accounting and document that a capped branch scan may re-examine fork hits on the next page.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment06.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the E5 "never a hang" guarantee is not enforceable — one record can blow the wall-clock budget**

The comment frames this cap as the E5 DoS bound, but a text-length cap is not a time bound on a backtracking regex engine (the Dart VM's `RegExp` backtracks — catastrophic patterns like `(a+)+$` over the 128 KB record are effectively unbounded). The time-budget check (`checkDeadline`) only runs **between** lines/blocks, never inside `pattern.hasMatch`, so a single pathological match on one giant record wedges the tool call — and the cancel token is not consulted during `execute` either — far beyond the promised 10 s, producing a hung agent rather than an "honest `truncated` report".

This matters more here than for a plain grep tool because the regex comes from the model itself, which routinely emits accidentally-quadratic patterns, and this PR's headline scenario is giant records.

Directions: bound the regex subject far smaller (a match over the first N KB of the record's preview-sized excerpt is enough for a pointer), or run the match in an isolate that can be abandoned on deadline expiry, or explicitly scope the E5 claim down to "budget checked between records" and cap per-record regex input accordingly.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment07.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: accumulator state grows linearly with archive size — the flat-memory claim (E4) does not hold**

`scanSessionSegment`'s doc claims "memory stays flat regardless of file size (E4)", and that is true only for the block/carry streaming. The accumulator itself retains per-record state for the whole chain: `_parentOf` for **every** record id (plus `_ordinalOf` in map mode, doubling it). For a multi-GB archive — this PR's explicit target — with a few million records this is hundreds of MB of id→parent pairs held for the entire scan, and it also accumulates identically on every continuation page.

Directions: the branch walk only needs parents of records on the leaf→root path. Since `RangedReadFileSystem` supports ranged reads, consider a two-pass approach (find the leaf in pass 1 storing only checkpoint/parent facts sparsely, then walk backwards in ranges), or keep parents only for records at/after the last observed fork, or correct the doc comment to state the linear bound honestly and decide whether it is acceptable for the E4 giant-session scenario.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment08.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the human-readable outcome of `recordPendingWait` is constructed and then discarded**

`recordPendingWait`'s doc says failures are "REPORTED here and swallowed by the afterToolCall wrapper" — but the wrapper (`_attachObligationPendingWaits`) awaits the result and drops it on the floor: nothing is ever reported anywhere, and all the outcome strings (`'pending-wait already recorded…'`, `'did not carry a scheduled id…'`, the swallow-message) are dead text. As written, a silent permanent failure (e.g. the schedule_message result wording changes — see the regex coupling note) is indistinguishable from success.

Either log the outcome through the CLI's logger/bus inside the wrapper, or drop the return value and simplify `recordPendingWait` to `Future<void>` so the code says what it does.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment09.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: only the `result cap` stop carries a continuation token — time-budget stops cannot be paged**

`nextContinuation` is set exclusively when `_stopReason == 'result cap'`. A scan stopped by the 10 s budget mid-archive gets `truncated: true` with no token, so the model's only recourse is the footer advice to narrow with `kinds`/`before`/`after` — fine for specific queries, but for a broad recall sweep over a multi-GB chain there may be no narrowing that fits the budget, and the agent is stuck re-scanning from the start each call (where it will time out again at roughly the same place, since the skip only honors the token).

Since `_skipped` already implements absolute-record skipping, the token is computable for any clean stop: consider `nextContinuation = recordsTotal - 1` (or `recordsTotal`, boundary semantics permitting) whenever the stop was not an error, and extend the footer to offer continuation for `time budget` too.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment11.md"}

Since `branch` is the **default** scope, every match on an abandoned fork consumes budget and can trigger a premature `result cap` that returns far fewer than 40 branch hits — or zero — while reporting `truncated: true`. Worse, the continuation token skips records globally, so each next page re-scans the entire prefix of the chain: paging through a fork-heavy giant session is O(n²) under a 10 s budget.

No test covers branch-scope + cap together (the seeded fork record doesn't match the test query, so the E4 test can't see this).

Directions: collect hits with branch membership decided at collection time where possible, or over-collect with slack and continue scanning when the branch-filtered count is below the cap; alternatively exclude non-branch hits from the cap accounting and document that a capped branch scan may re-examine fork hits on the next page.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment06.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the E5 "never a hang" guarantee is not enforceable — one record can blow the wall-clock budget**

The comment frames this cap as the E5 DoS bound, but a text-length cap is not a time bound on a backtracking regex engine (the Dart VM's `RegExp` backtracks — catastrophic patterns like `(a+)+$` over the 128 KB record are effectively unbounded). The time-budget check (`checkDeadline`) only runs **between** lines/blocks, never inside `pattern.hasMatch`, so a single pathological match on one giant record wedges the tool call — and the cancel token is not consulted during `execute` either — far beyond the promised 10 s, producing a hung agent rather than an "honest `truncated` report".

This matters more here than for a plain grep tool because the regex comes from the model itself, which routinely emits accidentally-quadratic patterns, and this PR's headline scenario is giant records.

Directions: bound the regex subject far smaller (a match over the first N KB of the record's preview-sized excerpt is enough for a pointer), or run the match in an isolate that can be abandoned on deadline expiry, or explicitly scope the E5 claim down to "budget checked between records" and cap per-record regex input accordingly.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment07.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: accumulator state grows linearly with archive size — the flat-memory claim (E4) does not hold**

`scanSessionSegment`'s doc claims "memory stays flat regardless of file size (E4)", and that is true only for the block/carry streaming. The accumulator itself retains per-record state for the whole chain: `_parentOf` for **every** record id (plus `_ordinalOf` in map mode, doubling it). For a multi-GB archive — this PR's explicit target — with a few million records this is hundreds of MB of id→parent pairs held for the entire scan, and it also accumulates identically on every continuation page.

Directions: the branch walk only needs parents of records on the leaf→root path. Since `RangedReadFileSystem` supports ranged reads, consider a two-pass approach (find the leaf in pass 1 storing only checkpoint/parent facts sparsely, then walk backwards in ranges), or keep parents only for records at/after the last observed fork, or correct the doc comment to state the linear bound honestly and decide whether it is acceptable for the E4 giant-session scenario.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment08.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the human-readable outcome of `recordPendingWait` is constructed and then discarded**

`recordPendingWait`'s doc says failures are "REPORTED here and swallowed by the afterToolCall wrapper" — but the wrapper (`_attachObligationPendingWaits`) awaits the result and drops it on the floor: nothing is ever reported anywhere, and all the outcome strings (`'pending-wait already recorded…'`, `'did not carry a scheduled id…'`, the swallow-message) are dead text. As written, a silent permanent failure (e.g. the schedule_message result wording changes — see the regex coupling note) is indistinguishable from success.

Either log the outcome through the CLI's logger/bus inside the wrapper, or drop the return value and simplify `recordPendingWait` to `Future<void>` so the code says what it does.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment09.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: only the `result cap` stop carries a continuation token — time-budget stops cannot be paged**

`nextContinuation` is set exclusively when `_stopReason == 'result cap'`. A scan stopped by the 10 s budget mid-archive gets `truncated: true` with no token, so the model's only recourse is the footer advice to narrow with `kinds`/`before`/`after` — fine for specific queries, but for a broad recall sweep over a multi-GB chain there may be no narrowing that fits the budget, and the agent is stuck re-scanning from the start each call (where it will time out again at roughly the same place, since the skip only honors the token).

Since `_skipped` already implements absolute-record skipping, the token is computable for any clean stop: consider `nextContinuation = recordsTotal - 1` (or `recordsTotal`, boundary semantics permitting) whenever the stop was not an error, and extend the footer to offer continuation for `time budget` too.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment11.md"}
